response: Yes, preoperative statins have been shown to reduce the incidence of atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Several studies have demonstrated that patients who are taking statins before undergoing CABG have a lower risk of developing postoperative atrial fibrillation, which is a common complication of cardiac surgery. The exact mechanism is not fully understood, but it is thought that statins may help to reduce inflammation and oxidative stress, which can contribute to the development of atrial fibrillation. As a result, many cardiologists and cardiac surgeons recommend continuing or initiating statin therapy before CABG to help reduce the risk of postoperative atrial fibrillation.
